items.rationale: Manually re-read all eight actual canonical CMS source-map sections and the current frozen manifest, delivery, dependency and localization owners. The article's authoring/delivery/manifest/migration/cache/governance separation remains accurate; no canonical article blocks changed. The new documentationNavigationProperties branch derives navigation metadata only from active reachable documentation articles in the exact preloaded Site/locale/channel/access scope, rejects absent/redirected/ambiguous identities, matches canonical code and route and uses only frozen localization variants. It performs no reads, imports, persistence, permission changes or approval. Existing manifest integrity, exact-version dependency loading and delivery pointer authority remain intact. Source-level projection rules are now explicit in the owning publication-manifest contract; this source-editorial pass does not assert the canonical overview contains a detailed new navigation tutorial or qualify native/browser behavior.

The documentation navigation renderer alone receives a detached nested item projection with current canonical title/summary/searchKeywords/searchText before that existing delivery projection.
persist/importManifest retain deterministic contentHash and immutable identity; activateScope checks pointer revision and propagates transactionContext. No global atomicity claim is added.

resolvePage uses immutable Online manifests only with cms.publication.enabled; employee shared composition rejects the legacy path. The article explicitly separates those paths and optional invalidation from actual cache freshness.

documentationNavigationProperties indexes only the supplied models, follows active frozen component associations through active pages/components with a seen set, and admits only non-redirect active routes matching Site, locale, channel and accessMode exactly. It requires a documentation article renderer, canonical code, declared source owner and matching article/navigation route; duplicate canonical identities become non-navigable rather than selecting an owner.

Navigation item order/identity and existing authored fields are retained, while title/summary/keywords/full-text come from the eligible current article and its existing governed localization resolver. Missing full text falls back only to current title/summary/keywords; missing or ambiguous article evidence drops the item, never revives historical navigation text.

buildSnapshot supplies only tenant/auth/transaction-scoped exact dependency versions loaded with active:true. The dependency adapter retains configured graph/depth/site limits and localization READY validation. The helper creates no new loader, latest lookup, data import, persistence access, authorization grant or executable route.

Existing immutable manifests and authored/shared release bytes are not rewritten. A newly reviewed publication snapshot gains the projection through the normal revision-pinned validation/Process approval path; the current Online pointer remains authoritative until ordinary publication succeeds.
correctnessAndCoverageLimitations: Optional nCache absence can return success without invalidating a cache; external CDN/browser freshness requires target evidence.
Migration rollback and publication pointer rollback are distinct recovery operations.

Projection qualification is source/local-fixture only. Native delivery must independently demonstrate newly approved exact manifest scope and navigation searchText equals the canonical article. A browser still applies its own bounded item-text filter, so source full-text projection is not proof every late-position keyword is discoverable.

The helper consumes already admitted frozen dependencies and canonical route access classifications; source.owner is provenance, not an independent access grant. Existing publication, identity, localization and delivery authorities remain required.
Large-site maximum-bound performance and browser search behavior were not benchmarked or accepted by this review.
